newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Berendsen to meet 1996 outlook.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Berendsen to meet 1996 outlook.

text.p: Analysts expect the 1996 result of Denmark's Sophus Berendsen A/S to match the company's own, donwgraded forecast of a 145 million crown profit before tax and associated company earnings, a Reuter consensus poll of eight analysts shows.
"But then it should, as the company's latest forecast was in November 1996," an analyst said.
Berendsen is to publish 1996 results on April 10.
Another analyst, who like his colleagues requested anonymity, said that he expected a more positive, 1997 forecast to accompany the 1996 report.
"We expect that Sophus Berendsen in its prognosis will announce an improvement and that 1997 will be a more normal operating year, without such large one-off expenses," he said.
The average forecast was for 146 million crowns and predictions ranged from a low of 142 million to an upper limit of 151 million crowns.

The company, 35.8 percent owner of Britain's Rentokil, issued a profits warning in November 1996 saying that it expected a 47 percent downturn in 1996 from 1995 due to losses in its Electronics and Data division.
Including the contributions of Rentokil and other associated companies the analysts predicted an average 1996 pre-tax profit of 1.294 billion crowns, rising to 1.844 billion in 1997.
